CORE DEFINITION

Behavioral Table of Elements

B-TOE

A two-axis field chart. Vertical = body region (head to feet). Horizontal = stress & deception likelihood, rising left to right. Every cell carries 14 data points.

Head-to-toe gestures, plus object interaction and verbal-expression syntax.

The Key: 14 Data Points Per Cell

Reference + Symbol

Stable location number and memorized abbreviation, e.g. 'acc.' for arm cross.

Confirming & Amplifying

Gestures that confirm a read (Fw → Cl, Jp) or amplify its meaning (Lc → Ct, Shg).

Deception Rating

0–4.0 score with B/D/A timeframe. 4.0 = extremely deceptive; 1.0 = not likely.

Myth vs Fact

MYTH
Baselining is unreliable — subjects fake it, so skip it.
FACT
Baseline everyone. Faked gestures conflict across cells and raise red flags anyway.
Gather data before high-stress questions; deceptive baselining is itself a signal.

Field Interrogation

PROBLEM

One question: 'Did anything happen in the car?' The suspect's own denial was the tell.

SOLUTION

Documented each gesture against the BToE: résumé statement, non-contracted denial, single-sided shrug, head shake, palm exposure.

KEY IMPACT & PROOF
4.0×3: Résumé, non-contraction, shrug  •  17.5: Total deception score (12 = extreme)  •  DNL: Palm exposure flagged as not-likely

One response, five signals, score 17.5 — a single question can expose a deceptive cluster.

Six Observation-Influencing Factors

Six Observation-Influencing Factors

Temperature (every 10° below 69° strips 1 point from closed gestures), interviewer behavior (each confrontational act −2 from 4.0-rated cells), subject emotional state (fear, aggression, defensiveness), proxemics, handicaps, and the presence of others. Non-measurable effects must be annotated in the report so human factors stay visible.

Field FAQs

Q1

Does hypnosis exist?

The book reframes it: the brain's autopilot handles obedience — influence works on that system.

Q2

Why baseline at all?

Deceptive baselining leaks intent; conflicting gestures raise red flags across cells.

Q3

One gesture = deception?

Never. A single shrug is innocuous alone; clusters of high-rated behaviors confirm.

Q4

Judgment during interviews?

Suspend it. Opinions corrupt the profile and can end with someone getting hurt.
